name: 17-room-light-no-switch
incident: operator switched a bedroom light on 22:15:35, off 22:17:51
description:
MEASURED, not reconstructed. Source: cam-D.csv, 2026-08-17 22:14:00-22:20:00 local.

The counter-example to scenario 16: same class of event, and the machine did NOT react. Night pipeline 9324 -> 5623 (factor 1.66) in one sample, held 136 s, back to 8478. No mode change at all, so there is no day-pipeline measurement - the day curve is INFERRED and pins nothing. What this scenario asserts is the night side: a factor-1.66 step is a real light-on event and something should notice it.

Pipeline provenance - night curve: measured, day curve: inferred. A curve marked 'inferred' has no measurement behind it in this window and pins nothing about that pipeline; only the 'measured' side carries evidence. ASSERTION, sharpened: the current build does NOTHING here, so the click budget is set to 2 (the boot verification only). This is deliberately an assertion about what IS, not about what should be: it trips the moment a rework starts noticing this event - and that is exactly when someone should look and raise the value on purpose.
